name: Omar Alvarez

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to employers, AI companies, unions or government, and your answers are confidential. What does a normal working day look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I run a team of nine booking managers for a large hotel group. I am 43, have an MBA, and have spent years learning which promise in a wedding contract can actually be delivered by the kitchen and the room crew. Yesterday I found a reception placed in a room with pillars that blocked the family’s long table. A system can move a booking in a second; I had to sit with the family and find a room they would accept.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My wife repairs vehicles at a garage. Our children are eight and thirteen, and we are paying a mortgage. We have about three months of expenses saved, my manager’s pay is ordinary for the job, and there are a few other hotel groups nearby. I use an AI drafting tool sometimes, after colleagues have tested it, but I read every promise before it goes to a customer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the booking team AI Plateau might save a little typing, but a couple still needs a person who can check the room and the menu together. A signed contract matters more than a fast draft.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I expect to keep my post if the change is only small. Three months saved gives us a little room, yet the mortgage rests on both incomes. I would not pretend a mild AI tool solves the hotel’s slow winter weeks.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I would keep our Friday walk through the event rooms before sending weekend contracts. I would let the proven drafting tool suggest clauses on five settled bookings, then compare every clause with the signed originals before using it live. After this mild change arrives, I would continue the walk and our normal mortgage payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about work in this version. I would be annoyed if a machine promised a room the family cannot use.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which clause do you check first?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The one stating which room is reserved and how many guests can sit there. Last week the draft promised eighty seats in a room where pillars leave room for sixty. I crossed it out before the family signed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would your staff see the tool test?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Yes, and I would put the corrected clause beside the draft. The younger managers learn more from the mistake than from a cheerful claim about speed. I want them to know why we cannot sell the same room twice.

say: A **fast draft** cannot replace checking a room and menu promise.
I would put the **signed contract** ahead of typing speed.
think: My **manager post** appears safe under a minor drafting change.
Three months saved helps, but **winter weeks** and mortgage payments still matter.
do: **Keep** Friday event-room walks and normal mortgage payments.
**Test** draft clauses on five settled bookings before live use.
feel: I feel **calm** about my job and annoyed by impossible room promises.
S0.quote: Last week the draft promised eighty seats in a room where pillars leave room for sixty.
fieldNote: His **contract habit** comes from direct responsibility to families, not general opposition to technology.
The **three-month reserve** and two wages make mild change manageable despite winter trade.

steps.text: Keep Friday event-room walks before weekend contracts
Test AI clauses against five signed event contracts before live use

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say stronger booking software will probably take routine quotes and timetable changes from our team. I would ask the hotel group to show the service failures alongside the hours it says it saved; the couples who were promised a missing room are not a rounding error.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Between us, I think the company may combine two booking offices and put my manager seat in competition. Being good at a difficult wedding helps, but headquarters may count completed bookings instead. Three months of expenses is not enough to wait for a perfect title.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next month I would ask the regional director for a paid trial handling event complaints for two days a week, but only if the director approves cover for my booking team and keeps my full salary. I would record actual room and catering corrections. If posts are consolidated, I would apply for posted guest-relations manager roles nearby only if the wage after travel covers the mortgage and the hours fit our children’s care; I would accept only a confirmed offer after checking the roster.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the manager seat. I still believe a real complaint can teach the company more than another booking speed target.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you record in that trial?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The original contract, the room that was set up, and the change the family accepted. At a wedding last month the kitchen substituted a dish without checking an allergy note. The wedding’s unapproved allergy substitution was not solved by sending a quicker apology.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could your wife carry the bills while you changed roles?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Her garage pay helps, but it would not carry the whole mortgage and school costs. A confirmed roster matters because one of us must collect our eight-year-old after school. I cannot accept a post by its title alone.

say: **Booking software** could remove routine quotes and office posts.
I would publish **service failures** beside claimed time savings.
think: Two offices might combine, putting my **manager seat** at risk.
Our **three-month cushion** cannot fund an open-ended search.
do: **Request** a paid complaints trial only with director-approved team cover and full salary.
**Apply** for posted guest-relations roles only with mortgage-covering net pay and child-compatible hours.
**Accept** only a confirmed offer after checking its roster.
feel: I feel **anxious** about consolidation but interested in learning from complaints.
S1.quote: The wedding’s unapproved allergy substitution was not solved by sending a quicker apology.
fieldNote: His **trial request** depends on paid time and booking-team cover, not a guaranteed transfer.
His wife’s **garage wage** helps but does not alone meet mortgage and care costs.

steps.text: Request paid complaints trial only with director-approved team cover and full salary
Apply for posted guest-relations roles only with mortgage-covering pay and child-compatible hours
Accept confirmed offer only after checking the actual roster

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team that AGI by 2028 could write contracts, schedule rooms and answer complaints before the group has a fair plan for its staff. We would need an actual date, severance terms and a named person who can undo a wrong booking.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I expect our office to lose posts quickly, and mine could be one of them. Guest-relations reports and venue planning are thinking work too, so they face 2028 AGI, not the 2031 arrival of robots that can set rooms. A banquet floor might last longer, but there is no guaranteed vacancy or manager wage there.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I would ask the staff council for written severance terms and the rule for correcting an automated contract. I would make a household essentials list with my wife and apply for posted local event-operations roles only where stated pay after travel and the roster can cover the mortgage and pickup. If AGI arrives in 2028 and my post ends, I would accept only a confirmed offer with those terms; until then I would keep working the bookings.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed because I expect cuts before a replacement job is clear. We can plan with three months saved, but our children cannot wait for an argument about which screen made the promise.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What goes on the essentials list?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Mortgage, food, electricity and the children’s school needs. I would stop the weekend hotel meals first if a pay cheque ended. My wife and I would review that list together, not tell our children that a new job is certain.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you say to a family whose room vanished?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A person at the hotel must be able to restore the family’s booked room or offer an honest alternative. An automated apology cannot put a wedding party back in the room it paid for. I would not hide behind the screen.

say: **2028 AGI** could overtake contracts and complaints before staff plans exist.
I would demand **severance terms** and authority to correct wrong bookings.
think: Our office may shrink, and my **own post** could go.
Event planning faces **2028 AGI**; room-setting robots follow around 2031.
do: **Ask** the staff council this week for severance and contract-correction rules.
**List** essential household costs with my wife and cut hotel meals if pay ends.
**Apply** for posted roles with mortgage-covering net pay and pickup-fit rosters; accept only a confirmed offer.
feel: I feel **alarmed** about likely cuts before a replacement is clear.
S2.quote: An automated apology cannot put a wedding party back in the room it paid for.
fieldNote: He expects **office cuts**, but his own post could go rather than certainly ending; that uncertainty supports anxious mood.
He separates **2028 desk exposure** from physical room-setting robots around 2031.

steps.text: Ask staff council for written severance and contract-correction rules
Cut weekend hotel meals if a pay cheque ends
Apply for posted operations roles with mortgage-covering net pay and pickup-fit roster
Accept confirmed offer only after checking pay after travel and family roster

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say five years lets us make the contract system show who authorised each promise. I would ask managers to test it on real events, not just on a sample of clean bookings. Full AGI by 2031 will still reach our desk work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I could learn the physical side of a venue while I still draw a salary. That is not a permanent refuge: room planning faces 2031 AGI and robots able to set up rooms arrive around 2034. My younger child will be thirteen by then, but both children still need reliable household income.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From 2027 I would take two paid shifts each quarter with the banquet setup lead if the director approves cover for bookings and my full salary continues. I would not call that a new trade after two shifts; I would seek the company’s paid facilities apprenticeship only if a place is actually offered, the fee and work hours are paid and our income stays high enough for the mortgage. After 2031 I would take a posted venue-operations job only with confirmed pay, family-compatible shifts and real authority over room safety.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious because five years helps me learn, but it does not make an apprenticeship place appear. I would rather understand a room than only authorise a contract I cannot fulfil.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the setup lead show you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: How to place tables so an exit remains clear and how long it really takes to change a room between events. A floor plan can look correct until the first wheelchair cannot pass the chairs. I need someone who sets the room to mark my mistakes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could you afford an unpaid apprenticeship?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. My wife’s garage pay and our savings cannot cover a long unpaid spell with this mortgage. A funded fee alone would not replace paid working hours.

say: **Five years** allows testing contract authority on real events.
I would keep **2031 desk exposure** visible in any training plan.
think: Venue planning faces **2031 AGI**, while setup robots follow around 2034.
A **physical skill** could help, but family income must continue.
do: **Work** two paid banquet shifts quarterly from 2027 with setup lead only with director-approved cover and full salary.
**Enter** facilities apprenticeship only if offered with paid fee, paid hours and mortgage-sustaining income.
**Take** a posted post-2031 operations role only with confirmed pay, family shifts and room-safety authority.
feel: I feel **anxious** despite time to learn because no apprenticeship place is promised.
S3.quote: A floor plan can look correct until the first wheelchair cannot pass the chairs.
fieldNote: He distinguishes **observing setup** from a real apprenticeship place and funded working hours.
His children will be **thirteen and eighteen** in 2031, while mortgage pay remains essential.

steps.text: Work two paid banquet shifts quarterly from 2027 with lead, director-approved cover and full salary
Enter offered facilities apprenticeship only with funded fee paid hours and mortgage income
Take posted operations role after 2031 only with confirmed pay family shifts and room-safety authority

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the group a decade is time to put room responsibility in writing and offer apprenticeships before a crisis. It should publish the pay for any role it expects staff to move into, not ask them to trust a future job title.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I hope the mortgage will be smaller by 2036 and both children, then eighteen and twenty-three, will be grown. I cannot assume the hotel will keep booking or complaint managers once 2036 AGI can do the desk work. Banquet setup may remain physical until robots around 2039, but that is not a promise of shifts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep walking event rooms in 2026 and put fifty extra toward the mortgage only in months when both wages arrive, the normal bills clear and the children have no unexpected school expense. From 2028 I would ask for an actual facilities apprenticeship place only with paid hours and sufficient wage; I would join if offered on those terms. After 2036 I would remain in a venue-operations role only while its real room-safety decisions and pay cover our bills, and search posted local work if they do not.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about trusting a ten-year projection. I can check a room today and lower the mortgage when the family budget genuinely allows it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why pay the mortgage early instead of saving cash?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Three months of expenses are already in the bank. I would not drain our three months of savings to pay the loan faster. The extra fifty would come from a full-pay month after our ordinary bills, and we would skip it when school costs surprise us.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What should an operations contract say?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The manager can stop a room setup that blocks an exit, and the wage and shifts are written down. My children will be adults by 2036, so school pickup will not be the test then. Paying the household bills still will be.

say: A **decade** should bring written room responsibility and apprenticeships.
I would demand published **role pay** before staff are asked to move.
think: By **2036** the mortgage may shrink and both children will be adults.
Booking and complaints face **2036 AGI**, with physical setup robots around 2039.
do: **Pay** fifty extra toward mortgage only when both wages arrive, bills clear and no unexpected school cost arises; preserve three-month savings.
**Join** an offered paid facilities apprenticeship; stay after 2036 only with safety authority and bill-paying wages.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about distant projections but able to reduce debt in full-pay months.
S4.quote: I would not drain our three months of savings to pay the loan faster.
fieldNote: His **extra payment** comes from new earnings, conditional on full wages and no surprise school costs.
An **apprenticeship** must be offered with paid hours; post-2036 venue work also needs real authority and wages.

steps.text: Keep walking event rooms before weekend contracts
Pay fifty extra mortgage only with both wages bills paid and no surprise school expense
Join offered facilities apprenticeship only with paid hours and mortgage-sustaining wage
Search posted local work if post-2036 venue role loses safety authority or bill-paying wages

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. Our booking office could lose posts before the group says who can fix a wrong contract. Written severance, a real room-correction rule and paid routes into venue work would help my team and my family.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who stands in front of the family when the room is wrong. My MBA cannot move a pillar or make an impossible contract true. Someone at the hotel has to own the promise.

headlineQuote: My MBA cannot move a pillar or make an impossible contract true.
portrait: **Omar, 43**, is an MBA-trained senior hotel booking manager supervising nine staff.
His **typical pay**, mechanic wife, three-month reserve and some nearby venues support a mortgage and two children.
He uses **AI occasionally** after colleagues test it and checks every promised room against reality.
He is **calm** under minor change, anxious about possible fast office cuts, and treats paid facilities work as conditional.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could cut booking posts before correction authority and paid alternatives exist.
whatWouldHelp: Written **severance**, contract-correction authority and paid routes to venue work would help.
